example.title: Florschuetz 1981 jet array
example.source: Florschuetz, L. W., Truman, C. R., Metzger, D. E. (1981). Streamwise flow and heat transfer distributions for jet array impingement with crossflow. ASME J. Heat Transfer 103, 337-342.
example.reproduced: The paper's rig: a jet plate fed from one plenum, ten spanwise rows of 0.1 in holes, the spent air leaving in one direction down the gap. Geometry B(5,4)I at z/d = 2 (xn/d 5, yn/d 4). The network solves the jet flow split; each row reads its own crossflow-to-jet ratio Gc/Gj from it and its Nu from the paper's correlation.
example.where_to_look: Solve, then select the impingement array. Its Per Row table shows Gc/Gj building up from 0 at row 1 to about 0.65 at row 10 (the paper's Eq. 8 gives the same to 1%) and Nu falling from row 1 as the crossflow grows. Fig. 6 of the paper plots the measured Nu/Nu1 against that Gc/Gj: 2% mean error at this geometry.
example.label: fidelity
example.label_note: Compared with the authors' own measured data (Fig. 6, digitised), so a miss is the implementation's to explain. All nine Fig. 6 panels: +4.0% bias, 6.9% mean error over 242 points.
